articles.title: UN Nuclear Watchdog Warns North Korea Has Built a New Facility to Make Nuclear Fuel
articles.summary: The United Nations' nuclear monitoring agency has announced that North Korea appears to have constructed a brand-new facility designed to enrich uranium — a key material used in making nuclear weapons. Inspectors spotted the site using satellite images. North Korea has been banned from developing nuclear weapons under international rules, but the country has repeatedly ignored these restrictions over many years. Experts say that having more enrichment sites makes it harder for the world to track how much nuclear material North Korea is producing. World leaders are calling for diplomacy to address the growing concern.

lv1: What has the UN's nuclear watchdog found that North Korea has built? (聯合國核監察機構發現北韓建造了什麼？)
What is uranium used for in this news story? (在這則新聞中，鈾被用來做什麼？)
lv2: Why is it a problem for the world if North Korea builds more places to make nuclear fuel? (如果北韓建造更多製造核燃料的地方，為什麼對世界來說是個問題？)
How do inspectors find out about secret facilities in another country without going there in person? (視察人員如何在不親身前往的情況下，發現另一個國家的秘密設施？)
lv3: Some people argue that countries should have the right to defend themselves with any weapons they choose, while others say nuclear weapons make the world more dangerous for everyone. Which view do you find more convincing, and why? (有些人認為國家有權選擇任何武器自衛，另一些人則認為核武器使全世界更危險。你認為哪種觀點更具說服力，為什麼？)

International sanctions have not stopped North Korea from expanding its nuclear programme for decades. Does this suggest that sanctions are an ineffective tool of diplomacy? What alternatives might work better? (國際制裁數十年來未能阻止北韓擴展其核計劃。這是否說明制裁是無效的外交工具？有什麼替代方案可能更有效？)

articles.title: World-Famous Japanese Artist Yayoi Kusama Dies at Age 97
articles.summary: Yayoi Kusama, one of Japan's most celebrated artists known for covering everything in colourful polka dots and bold patterns, has passed away at the age of 97. She became famous around the world for her unique style — filling rooms, sculptures, and canvases with repeating dots and bright colours. Kusama began making art as a child to cope with difficult feelings, and eventually moved to New York to share her work globally. She remained creative right up until her final years. Her exhibitions attracted millions of visitors across Asia, Europe, and the Americas, inspiring countless young artists.

lv1: How old was Yayoi Kusama when she passed away? (草間彌生去世時幾歲？)
What was the most recognisable feature of Yayoi Kusama's artwork? (草間彌生藝術作品最具代表性的特點是什麼？)
lv2: Why do you think Yayoi Kusama's colourful dot-filled artwork became popular with people all over the world? (你認為為什麼草間彌生充滿彩色圓點的藝術作品會在全世界受到歡迎？)
Kusama used art to help manage her emotions since childhood. How can creative activities like drawing or music help people deal with their feelings? (草間彌生從小就用藝術幫助自己管理情緒。像繪畫或音樂這樣的創意活動怎樣幫助人們處理感受？)
lv3: Yayoi Kusama's art has been turned into hugely popular Instagram-worthy exhibitions that sell expensive tickets. Does commercialising art in this way make it more accessible to ordinary people, or does it betray the original spirit of artistic expression? (草間彌生的藝術被轉化為廣受歡迎、適合在社交媒體打卡的展覽，並出售昂貴門票。這種將藝術商業化的方式，是令藝術更平易近人，還是背叛了藝術表達的原始精神？)

Kusama spent much of her life living in a psychiatric institution by choice, yet became one of the world's most influential artists. What does her story tell us about the relationship between mental health, creativity, and society's expectations of 'normal' life? (草間彌生自願在精神病院度過了大半生，卻成為世界上最具影響力的藝術家之一。她的故事告訴我們，精神健康、創造力與社會對「正常」生活的期望之間有什麼關係？)

articles.title: 李家超今日發表香港首個五年規劃及2026年施政報告
articles.summary: 行政長官李家超今日（9月16日）在立法會發表香港歷史上首個「五年規劃」（2026至2030年），並同步公布2026年《施政報告》。今次規劃涵蓋住屋、交通、人口、北部都會區發展等多個重要範疇。社會各界高度關注政府會否延續生育津貼、重推租置計劃，以及港珠澳大橋能否實現「車上無感通關」等新措施，以應對香港面對的人口老化及經濟挑戰。

lv1: 李家超今日發表的是哪兩份重要文件？
香港首個五年規劃涵蓋哪些年份？
lv2: 為什麼政府需要制定五年規劃？提前計劃對香港有什麼好處？
「人口老化」對香港社會可能帶來哪些挑戰？
lv3: 政府提供生育津貼以鼓勵市民生育，你認為這類措施真的能有效解決香港人口下降的問題嗎？除此之外，還有什麼方法可以應對人口老化？
香港首個五年規劃的制定，有人認為有助長遠穩定發展，也有人擔心政策缺乏靈活性。你認為政府應如何在長遠規劃與靈活應變之間取得平衡？

articles.title: 港珠澳橋擬推「車上無感通關」　施政報告料涵蓋多項創新科技措施
articles.summary: 據悉，2026年《施政報告》將提出多項善用創新科技的新政策，其中包括港珠澳大橋實現「智通行」車上無感通關，讓車輛毋須在口岸停車接受人工查驗，大幅縮短過關時間。此外，報告料亦涉及太空經濟、人工智能及知識產權等新興產業的發展方向，以推動香港成為國際創新科技中心。有關措施反映政府致力透過科技提升市民生活及強化香港的競爭力。

lv1: 「施政報告」提到哪條大橋將試行新通關方式？
lv2: 「車上無感通關」採用了哪類科技？這種科技如何令過關更快捷方便？
為什麼香港政府希望發展太空經濟和人工智能產業？這對香港未來有什麼影響？
lv3: 利用科技進行自動通關雖然方便，但同時涉及收集大量個人資料。你認為在提升效率與保障私隱之間，應如何取得平衡？
香港致力發展成為「國際創新科技中心」，但面對來自深圳、新加坡等城市的競爭。你認為香港有哪些獨特優勢，又有哪些需要改善的地方？
